Fictional teaching universe · synthetic data

Come with a degree.Leave with a portfolio.

You already have the qualification, or the job. What you don't have is the evidence. Every path here puts you inside a working organisation — a hospital, a university, a bank — with a real brief from a real desk. You leave with work you can show: for the interview, for the promotion, or for your own venture.

You have a degreeand the theory. What's missing is anything an employer can look at.
You're already workingand want the next role. You need a case, not a certificate.
You want to buildsomething of your own. Start from a friction someone actually has.

The block

Three organisations, one street

click a building to go in · click a person to meet who you'll be

How a path works

Ten credits, start to portfolio

  1. Pick a worldHospital, university or bank. The domain decides whose desk you sit at, not how hard the work is.
  2. Take a briefA named person with a real friction hands you a problem. Dana's Thursday gap. Lucas's week-3 cliff. Ji-woo's delinquency drift.
  3. Build the three artifactsThe data model, the model, the agent workflow. Each is assessed on whether a working professional would accept it.
  4. Pick your exitInterview, growth role, or founder. Same three artifacts, three different things to do with them.
  5. Leave with the workNot a transcript. A portfolio, a recorded defence, and the vocabulary to hold a conversation with the people who hire.

The shape of a path

Where the ten credits go

90 guided hours · ~20 weeks · ~4.5 hrs a week

Ten credits is the cap, and the arithmetic only closes one way: three courses at 2 credits, two at 1, four at 0.5. At nine guided hours per credit that is 90 hours over about 20 weeks — roughly four and a half hours a week, which is what a working adult can actually hold.

What you leave with

Three artifacts, one from each major

01

A data model you can defend

A documented extract — grain, joins, definitions — and the review it passed. This is the artifact that survives the hardest interview question: why is this number right?

02

A model with its failure modes named

Calibrated, thresholded against a stated cost, with subgroup performance reported before deployment rather than after. Accuracy alone impresses nobody who hires for this.

03

An agent workflow that survived a fact-check

A four-step agent week with its folders scoped and a verification gate at each stage — the thing most candidates talk about and almost none can demonstrate.

Exit routes

Same portfolio, three destinations

The capstone carries no extra credit — the cap is the cap. The three 2-credit majors each contribute one artifact to it, and the exit route you pick decides what you do with those three artifacts in the final two weeks.

Interview

Portfolio review

You are applying, and you need something on the screen to talk about.

You do Package the three artifacts, record a ten-minute walkthrough, then defend one decision under questioning from someone who disagrees with it.

Graded on The defence, not the deliverable. A good artifact you cannot explain fails this.

Growth role

The funded proposal

You are already inside, and you want the next role.

You do Turn one story arc into a business case for a named decision-maker — Dr. Osei, Dr. Demirtaş or Hassan Rafiq — with cost, risk, and an honest downside scenario.

Graded on Whether that person would sign it. Proposals with no downside section do not pass.

Founder

The wedge

You want to build something of your own.

You do Take one friction from the cast and scope it as a product: who pays, what it replaces, what it costs to run, and the profile of the first customer who would switch.

Graded on The unit economics and the first customer. A market-size slide is not evidence.

Fictional universe · synthetic data · teaching use only

UCJersey Group

One invented city block, three institutions, every course taught inside it.

Learners meet a hospital, a university and a bank that share a founder, a data warehouse convention and a cast of people who recur by name. The clinical context is learned once; after that only the tooling changes. A learner who followed Dana through her Thursday gap already knows how to read Lucas's week-3 cliff — same shape of problem, different institution, different table names.

3institutionshospital, university, bank
60personasacross 18 departments
38warehouse tablesthree separate models
27courses mapped22 built, finance in design

Where it came from

UCJersey began in 1958 as a hospital, added an online university in 2009 to train the staff it could not recruit, and inherited the campus credit union in 1974 — which is why the Institute still runs the hospital's payroll. None of it is real. All of it is consistent, which is what makes it teachable.

Institutions

Pick a world

each one is a full scenario

Connections

How they touch each other

These four ties are what make a cross-institution capstone possible. Without them three scenarios would just be three unrelated datasets.

UCJ↔UCJMC

Practicum placements

Every health informatics learner does a practicum inside the Medical Center. Dr. Selin Kaya negotiates the placements; Dana Okonkwo and Wen Li host them.

UCJMC↔UCFI

Payroll and the float pool

The Institute has run the hospital's payroll since 1974. Shift and float data on one side, deposit timing and overdraft fees on the other.

UCJ↔UCFI

Tuition instalment plans

The Institute underwrites the university's instalment plans, so a learner's aid hold and their loan delinquency are two views of the same month.

UCJ↔UCJMC

The pipeline question

Both institutions want to know whether the practicum produces employees who stay. Neither can answer it from its own warehouse alone.

Tracks

Three tracks, one method

Same nine-step shape in every track: the domain, the data model, the language, the dashboard, the model, the hard modality, prompting, agents, delivery. Only the institution changes.

Hospital track

9 courses

For Clinical operations, health informatics, hospital analytics

Leaves with Can read a clinical data model, build the dashboard a unit director will use daily, and say what a model costs when it is wrong.

Education track

9 courses

For Registrars, student success, institutional research, learning design, edtech

Leaves with Can define retention defensibly, find the week-3 cliff in an event log, and tell a detector score from evidence.

Finance track

4 courses

For Credit risk, fraud operations, model risk, retail banking analytics

Leaves with Can build a scorecard, price a threshold in losses and false declines, and write an adverse-action reason that is true.

Capstones

Questions one warehouse cannot answer

3 cross-institution

The capstone is where the group structure earns its keep: the learner has to define a link between two organisations, defend it, and handle the ethics of joining the data at all.

UCJUCJMC

The Practicum Pipeline

Do practicum placements at UCJMC produce graduates who are still employed there two years later — and which units produce the ones who stay?

Needs Join enrolment and program (ucj_ed) to staff and shift_assignment (ucj_core). Neither warehouse answers it alone; the learner has to define the link and defend it.

UCJMCUCFI

Payday, Shifts and Overdrafts

Do staff on heavy float rotations hit overdraft fees more often than staff on fixed lines — and if so, is that a scheduling problem or a product problem?

Needs shift_assignment (ucj_core) against account and transaction (ucj_fin), aggregated so no individual is identifiable. The ethics review is part of the deliverable.

UCJUCFI

Aid Holds and Instalment Default

Does an aid disbursement hold predict a missed tuition instalment — and does the bank's collections call arrive before or after the university's advisor?

Needs financial_aid (ucj_ed) with payment_schedule and delinquency_event (ucj_fin). Two organisations, two calls, one person receiving both.

Canon rules

What stays true everywhere

Badge prefixes

UCU- for the university, UCJ- for the hospital, UCFI- for the Financial Institute. A four-digit block per department, so a badge number tells you where someone sits.

Everything is synthetic

No figure, name, record or rate comes from a real institution. Patients, learners and customers are only ever Patient A, Learner B, Customer C — never named, never given a backstory that could read as a real person.

One learner lens per track

Each institution carries one or two personas written as the seat a student sits in: Dana Okonkwo and Jamal Rivers at the hospital, Lucas Frey and Ethan Pardo at the university, Ji-woo Han at the Institute. Labs are written from their desk.

Every arc ends in a decision

An arc is not a topic. It closes with someone choosing: fund the role, change the threshold, sign the contract, drop the alert. That is what makes it gradeable.

The data model is small on purpose

Ten to fourteen tables per institution. Real enough to teach grain, joins and late-arriving rows; small enough for a beginner to hold in their head.

Governance is a character, not a chapter

Nathan Cole at the hospital, Gordon Whitlock at the university, Dr. Elias Braun at the Institute. Responsible AI shows up as a person with a job, in the room where the decision is made.

Using it

How to build a course from this

  1. Pick the institution, then the personaOpen the institution a course belongs to, filter the cast to the department the lesson concerns, and open one persona's file. That file is the brief.
  2. Copy the scenario brief into the promptEach persona detail panel carries a copyable brief — role, goals, frictions, systems, tables, voice. Paste it at the top of a course-authoring prompt and every lesson in that course stays consistent.
  3. Write labs from a learner lensAddress the lab to Dana, Lucas or Ji-woo. 'You are Lucas, it is Tuesday of week 3' beats 'consider a hypothetical program manager'.
  4. Take tables from the data model, not from imaginationIf a lab needs a column, add it to the institution's model here first. A course that invents a table breaks every other course that joins to it.
  5. End the assessment where the arc endsThe arc names the decision. Grade the learner on the decision and its defence, not on whether the query ran.

Why it exists

Online-first does not mean faceless. Every June the whole university meets for one residency week on a partner campus — poster sessions, live seminars, a cohort photo on the steps. Half these scenarios turn on the gap between what the LMS log records and what actually happened in someone's week.

Story arcs

What actually happens

8 arcs
Coordination

The Thursday Gap

Family Health loses provider coverage most Thursday afternoons. Nobody can prove it until the schedule, the no-show log and the inbox are read together.

080402
Creativity

The Float-MA Business Case

Dana has to turn the gap into a funded role. Five source files, one deck, one decision-maker who reads the appendix first.

080401
Clarity

Reading the Agency Contract

The staffing agency's MSA runs 34 pages. The cancellation window and the minimum-hours clause decide whether the pilot is affordable.

0801
Coaching

Rehearsing the Pitch

Twelve minutes with Dr. Osei and the CEO. Dana practises the objections before she hears them for real.

0809
Data

Critical Values That Went Unread

A potassium of 6.4 sat 91 minutes before callback. The lab has the timestamps; nobody had the query.

020304
Data

Readmissions on 4 West

11.2% against a 9.5% target. The model is the easy part; the threshold and who gets the call are not.

050307
Data

The Radiograph Worklist

Overnight chest films queue up in arrival order. Kwame wants them ordered by suspicion — and audited for who the model fails.

0603
Data

Denials and the Auth Clock

18.4% first-pass denial on imaging. Marcus knows the payers; the warehouse knows the turnaround hours.

010204
Fictional · synthetic data · teaching use onlyIn design — 4 of 9 courses written, 5.5 of 10 credits scoped

UCJersey Financial Institute

Community bank · former campus credit union · retail + small-business lending  ·  Jersey City, New Jersey — 9 branches, 1 digital channel  ·  est. 1974

$2.4bntotal assets78% funded by core deposits
141,000customers34% are university alumni
9branchesplus the app that does 81% of transactions
$780mconsumer loan bookauto, personal, card, tuition instalment
2.9%30+ day delinquencyrising from 2.1% last year
0.14%card fraud loss rateof authorised volume

Source systems

Corelink CoreAccounts, ledger, postings, statements
UCJ Lakehouse — FinNightly core + card extracts, 10 outline tables
Sentinel FraudReal-time card authorisation scoring
LoanPath LOSApplications, decisioning, documents
Recoveries DeskCollections queues, promises, arrangements
Power BI ServiceExec, credit and branch dashboards

Units & departments

Executive & Board RiskRetail Banking & BranchesDigital ChannelSmall Business LendingConsumer CreditCollections & RecoveriesFraud OperationsBSA/AML ComplianceModel Risk ManagementFinance & TreasuryData & Analytics

Why it exists

The Institute exists so the same analytics skills can be taught where the harm is financial rather than clinical: a wrong threshold denies someone credit instead of delaying a diagnosis. Fair-lending and model-risk review play the role that clinical governance plays at the Medical Center.

Story arcs

What actually happens

3 arcs
Data

The Delinquency Drift

30-day delinquency moved 2.1% to 2.9% in a year. Nobody can say whether it's the book, the economy, or a policy change in March.

0203
Data

Declined at the Till

The fraud model's new threshold cut losses 22% and generated 3,100 false declines a month. One of those was a customer's rent.

0304
Clarity

Explain the Decline

A declined applicant is owed specific reasons. The model gives a score; the letter needs sentences that are true.

0401

The UCJersey Group is fictional. Every institution, person, figure, unit and record here is invented for instruction. No real hospital, university, bank, patient, learner, customer or employee is represented, and no figure is drawn from real data. The universe exists so course examples stay consistent across SQL, Python, Power BI, machine learning, NLP, imaging and agentic AI — reuse the cast, the tables and the arcs freely inside the programme.
